Article Title: 'No compelling circumstance': SC declines to intervene in CJP's September 5 protest march
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to intervene against Cockroach Janata Party's protest march on September 5, saying that maintenance of law and order was primarily the responsibility of the government and police.A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana said that there is no reason to presume that the proposed demonstration would insult in any untoward incident."We will at least, as of now, presume everybody will behave in a peaceful manner. Right now there is no compelling circumstance to assume that any untoward thing will happen," the CJI observed.The bench issued notice to the Centre and Delhi Police and posted the next hearing for September 10, along with other matters concerning the student protests.This comes after a plea was filed by retired Delhi Police officer Rajendra Singh, seeking directions to ensure that large-scale demonstrations and protest marches in sensitive areas of the national capital are held only after obtaining requisite police permissions.The counsel, appearing for Singh, urged the apex court to hear the matter on September 3, citing the proposed march and the upcoming BRICS Summit in Delhi on September 12-13.The counsel referred to the violence during the July 20 Sansad March announced by the CJP and cautioned that another incident could occur, even if not directly attributable to the organisers.The CJI, however, said the court could not proceed on the assumption that something untoward would happen and reiterated that the police authorities were competent to deal with any law-and-order situation."Before us, there is no identified group. You please impress upon the Union or NCT Delhi. It's for them to maintain law and order. They should act as per law," the CJI said."They are expected to maintain law and order, and the enforcing agency has the responsibility to maintain law and order... We are expecting them to act within that framework. From both sides, we are expecting that they will respect, they will conduct themselves, and they will follow the law of the land...," he added.The CJP has announced the September 5 march in Delhi, alleging that the Centre failed to honour its commitment to withdraw cases against students who participated in the July protests over the alleged examination paper leak
Article Summary: The Supreme Court declined to intervene against Cockroach Janata Party's protest march on September 5. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana said that there is no reason to presume that the proposed demonstration would insult in any untoward incident. The bench issued notice to the Centre and Delhi Police and posted the next hearing for September 10.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday paid floral tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at his memorial in Bishkek and interacted with members of Indian and Kyrgyz communities ahead of the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit.PM Modi paid his respects at the Mahatma Gandhi memorial before participating in the SCO Summit in the Kyrgyz capital. The statue was unveiled by PM Modi during his visit to Kyrgyzstan in 2015.PM Modi also met members of various communities, including those associated with Indian culture, yoga and the Indian diaspora.During the interaction, PM Modi received a copy of Manas: Kyrgyz Veergatha Kavya from members of the community.Members of the Kyrgyz cultural and yoga communities also spoke about their participation in workshops and performances promoting Indian traditions, including Odissi and yoga.Danil Rykov, President of the Yoga Federation of Kyrgyzstan, said, "It's been an incredible joy for us. It's been such an honor to participate in the workshops and especially in the performance here. For us, to have the opportunity to share the same stage with these great maestros and outstanding personalities was an immense joy and we really believe that this can open up new opportunities for our future events, to increase this marvelous and beautiful collaboration between our associations and our cultures.Jyldyz Kuvatova, founder of the Art of Living Foundation in Kyrgyzstan and professor at the American University of Central Asia, said, "We're so excited to be here. In just four days, we had more than four hours of intensive workshops every day and we had meetings with great personalities, our teachers and the maestros. It was so intense, but it's so much worth it. And we had a performance, we're very excited and thank you for inviting us. "Hatha yoga instructor Arina Niiazbekova, who is also associated with classical theatre, ballet and Indian classical dance, said the workshops provided an opportunity to learn from renowned gurus and performers."I work in the theatre, classical theatre, and I am ballet soloist, teacher, choreographer and the leader of the classical group. And also I perform classical Indian dance. And today we are meeting for the festival. It was really exciting time and we performed today. I'm performing in front of great gurus, masters and great soloists. I was extremely happy to see old friends and new friends today here. I think it is very useful for each of us to have workshops like we had with gurus," she said.PM Modi also interacted with members of the Indian community in Bishkek.Aditya Bhushan Mitra, Director of Kyrgyzstan-based Pylon Traders, described his participation in the cultural programme as an "incredible experience"."Namaskar and it was an incredible experience being here. And also, for me, it was an incredible opportunity to learn from our teachers, from the great personalitiesand to show our culture and everything. It was just like a dream coming true," he said.According to the Ministry of External Affairs, PM Modi has arrived in Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Leadership Summit, which brings together 10 member states, 15 partner countries and two observer countries for discussions on regional and global issues.PM Modi is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the summit, including with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin.His visit to Bishkek is the second leg of his two-country tour following his State Visit to Uzbekistan, where he held talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.During the Uzbekistan visit, India and Uzbekistan elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and agreed to expand cooperation in areas including trade, investment, infrastructure, digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, energy, space, agriculture, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, education and culture.The two sides also set a target of increasing bilateral trade to USD 5 billion by 2030.Before leaving Tashkent, PM Modi thanked President Mirziyoyev for his hospitality, saying, "Thank you, Uzbekistan! Gratitude to President Mirziyoyev for his warmth, attention to detail, and personal commitment to the India-Uzbekistan friendship."During the visit, PM Modi also paid floral tribute to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri at the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent. "Paid homage to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji in Tashkent. We remember a towering statesman whose unwavering commitment to the nation continues to inspire generations," he said.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a plea seeking mandatory disclosure of the exact ethanol content in petrol at fuel stations and on fuel purchase receipts.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale dismissed the plea filed by advocate Narendra Goswami, while granting him liberty to approach the concerned high court.The Attorney General for India, R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, argued that the petition was a proxy litigation, as the court had already dismissed a similar petition on the issue."The petitioner wants government of India to be answerable to him," the AG submitted, as quoted by PTI.Meanwhile, Goswami contended that he has the right to know the content of the petrol given. "Not only me but citizens at large should be informed about the composition of the fuel given to them," he submitted.The plea sought directions to petrol pumps to prominently display the precise percentage of ethanol blended with petrol. It also sought that the ethanol content be specifically mentioned on receipts and invoices issued to consumers at fuel stations and an official vehicle-wise compatibility database covering different ethanol blends, based on factors such as manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture."Direct the respondents (Centre and others) to prepare and publish within a stipulated time an official, public, vehicle-wise compatibility database searchable by manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture, indicating the suitability or otherwise of various ethanol blends for each vehicle," Goswami added in his plea.The plea also called for an independent expert committee, including representatives from the petroleum and road transport ministries, the Bureau of Indian Standards and independent automobile engineers, to assess the real-world compatibility of E20 with existing vehicles.The committee was also asked to examine the impact of E20 on fuel efficiency, engine life and maintenance costs, warranty and insurance, emissions, water consumption in ethanol production, and food-security concerns.The petitioner further sought a national consumer disclosure protocol for ethanol-blended petrol and a transparent transition framework for older or incompatible vehicles, including the possible availability of lower-ethanol petrol where feasible.
Article Summary: The plea sought ethanol-content labelling at pumps and on bills, a vehicle-wise E20 compatibility database, and a transition plan for incompatible vehicles. The Attorney General for India, R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, argued that the petition was a proxy litigation.

Article Title: For every Rs 100 laundered, only Re 1 recovered by authorities: CJI
Article Text:
Economic crimes move faster than treaties; global cooperation key to recovery: CJI Surya Kant

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said for every Rs 100 laundered, authorities and law enforcement agencies recovered only Re 1, mainly because of the ingenuity of economic offenders, and lack of global cooperation on extraditing fugitives.Money laundered globally in a year was more than enough to buy every single person on earth a modest laptop, CJI said at the 43rd International Symposium on Economic Crime in Cambridge Saturday. "...For every hundred parts of that wealth, ninety-nine are simply referred to in speeches and reports, while only one part is ever actually put right."CJI Surya Kant quoted ancient Indian statesman Kautilya’s Arthashastra, which had recorded that it was impossible for an official to handle the king’s revenue and take nothing from it, and provided for an antidote through audits, cross-verification and confiscation of ill-gotten gain.Referring to India’s layered legislations against economic crimes and its balancing by judicial interventions, the CJI said though India had signed extradition and mutual legal assistance treaties with foreign jurisdictions, “the property we actually recover remains, frankly, underwhelming”.The CJI said that illicit wealth and economic crimes moved faster than the pace of ratification of treaties and, hence, no jurisdiction, however well resourced or determined, could pursue them alone, despite the existence of provisions for non-conviction based forfeitures, unexplained wealth orders, beneficial ownership registers and financial intelligence sharing.“None of these tools is missing from our shelves. What is missing, and what each jurisdiction owes the other, is the willingness to use them together rather than one at a time: a forfeiture order in one country acted upon promptly by a registry in another, an intelligence tip followed through to an actual freeze rather than left to gather dust,” he further added.India had initiated processes for extraditions of Vijay Mallya with the UK authorities in 2017 and Nirav Modi with the US in 2018.None of them has fructified in extradition of the two, accused of misappropriating huge sums and fleeing the country.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said for every Rs 100 laundered, authorities and law enforcement agencies recovered only Re 1. Money laundered globally in a year was more than enough to buy every single person on earth a modest laptop, CJI said.

Article Title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
Article Text:
In the case of Everest, FSSAI has prohibited the sale of compounded (hing powder) variants with immediate effect.

NEW DELHI: The humble pinch of hing used in Indian kitchens has come under the scanner, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issuing prohibition orders against Everest Food Products Private Limited and Laljee Godhoo and Company over non-compliance in compounded hing and asafoetida products. In a social media post, the food regulator said it had issued prohibition orders against the two companies under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. For Everest, samples of compounded asafoetida, yellow hing powder and black hing powder were found non-compliant with prescribed alcohol-soluble extract requirements. One sample recorded “zero per cent”, against required minimum of 5%, while yellow and black hing powder samples recorded 3.29% and 4.4%, respectively.The food regulator cited earlier compliance reviews that found violations in chicken masala, garam masala and egg curry powder, including label-declaration issues.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issues prohibition orders against Everest Food Products Private Limited and Laljee Godhoo and Company. Regulator cites earlier compliance reviews that found violations in chicken masala, garam masala and egg curry powder.

Article Title: NHAI mandates end-to-end AI-MC deployment for projects over 20 km in length

NEW DELHI: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has made Automated and Intelligent Machine-Aided Construction (AI-MC) compulsory for all highway projects longer than 20 km in length and costing over Rs 500 crore, in what’s a move aimed at addressing quality issues, which have become a major concern for govt.As per an NHAI circular issued on Friday, contractors will have to use the AI-MC system while building the road from the ground up and continuously across the entire spatial footprint of the project. The technology will be used for every major layer of highway, including embankment (raised earth foundation), subgrade (compacted soil base) and Granular Sub-Base (GSB) — the first layer of crushed stone, sand and gravel laid over the compacted soil before the road surface is built.The move is aimed at improving construction quality and ensuring roads are built with greater accuracy and uniformity. AI-MC is a construction technology with on-board computers and sensors on heavy machinery such as graders, pavers, compactors and dozers. Deployment of AI-MC aims to improve the quality, durability and transparency of road construction by replacing manual monitoring with technology-driven, real-time execution and quality control.TOI has learnt that though AI-MC was first deployed during construction of Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway, it was not used on the entire stretch and at all grades.Officials said the move is designed to minimise human errors, ensure uniform construction standards and generate digital records of every stage of construction, from earthwork to pavement laying. “The new norms make it mandatory to share real-time data with NHAI officials.This is good for contractors and for us as well. Once the contractor gets real-time data, there will be hardly any scope for sub-contractors to cut corners,” said an official.Some of the industry players in AI-MC segment said that contractors are reluctant to share real-time data with NHAI and other highway construction agencies as this makes them accountable. “Unless NHAI and other agencies get the data in real time, the impact of using the technology will be negligible. It must not be used in a piecemeal way if govt is serious about putting things in order,” said one of them.
Article Summary: NHAI has made Automated and Intelligent Machine-Aided Construction compulsory for all highway projects longer than 20 km. The move is aimed at improving construction quality and ensuring roads are built with greater accuracy and uniformity. AI-MC is a construction technology with on-board computers and sensors on heavy machinery.

Article Title: Indian Standard Time to become mandatory for all entities from March 2027
Article Text:
Govt notifies Legal Metrology (IST) Rules, 2026, making IST mandatory for all legal, commercial and administrative activities from March 2027.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From March next year, all entities in India will be required to use Indian Standard Time (IST) for legal, commercial, digital and administrative activities, with govt on Saturday notifying the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026.The rules, notified under the Legal Metrology Act, will come into force 180 days after their publication in Gazette, making IST mandatory from around March 2027. Violations of the rules will attract penalties under the Act.The notification makes IST the mandatory time reference for all legal, administrative and official documents unless specifically exempted. It also makes IST the standard time reference across commerce, transport, public administration, legal contracts and financial operations.Entities will not be allowed to use, display or record any time reference other than IST for official purposes, except where foreign time zones are clearly labelled or where alternative time sources are permitted for scientific research, navigation or astronomy.The rules are significant as modern digital infrastructure depends on microsecond-level timing accuracy. Payment systems, stock exchanges, telecom networks, 5G services, digital navigation, power grids and data centres require synchronised clocks to authenticate transactions, coordinate operations and maintain network reliability.The notification establishes a nationwide system for time synchronisation, traceability and cybersecurity, recognising accurate time as critical digital infrastructure. Under the rules, CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (NPL) will continue to maintain India’s primary time scale, UTC(NPLI), from which IST is derived, while Regional Reference Standards Laboratories (RRSLs), ISRO’s NavIC and other authorised timing sources will disseminate official time.Another major feature of the rules is the focus on cyber resilience. Organisations must deploy proper time-synchronisation systems, protect networks against spoofing, jamming and cyberattacks, integrate multiple authorised timing sources and maintain contingency mechanisms, including atomic clocks where necessary, to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Article Summary: Govt notifies Legal Metrology (IST) Rules, 2026, making IST mandatory for all legal, commercial and administrative activities from March 2027. Violations of the rules will attract penalties under the Act. The rules are significant as modern digital infrastructure depends on microsecond-level timing accuracy.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Reflecting India’s green energy push, renewable energy contributed nearly 20% of the country’s power generation in July and registered a year-on-year growth of over 30%.According to Grid India data, of the total power generation of 1,81,790 mw in July, 36,355 mw was sourced from solar, wind and biomass, which constitute renewable energy, accounting for 19.9% of the total generation. In comparison, 27,835 mw of the total 1,64,393 mw, or 16.9%, came from RE sources in July 2025.A power ministry official said the data showed that India’s efforts to move from fossil fuels to cleaner sources of energy were beginning to show results. “We aim to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070. Renewable energy now accounts for more than 42% of our total installed capacity of about 552 gw. If we include nuclear and hydro, our installed non-fossil capacity has reached about 295 gw,” the official said.Thermal sources, including coal and lignite, however, continue to provide the baseload power, accounting for 66% of the total generation, about 13% higher than last year.For only the second time ever, peak power demand crossed 270 gw in July, driven by hot and humid conditions across the country and the El Nino phenomenon. The share of hydropower in total generation was 10.2% in July 2026, lower than the 14.5% share recorded a year earlier. Except gas and hydro, all major fuels saw a year-on-year increase in power generation.
Article Summary: Renewable energy accounts for nearly 20% of India's power generation in July, up from 16.9% a year ago. For only the second time ever, peak power demand crossed 270 gw in July. The share of hydropower in total generation was 10.2% in July 2026, lower than 14.5% recorded a year earlier.

India and Uzbekistan upgraded their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, set an annual trade target of $ 5 billion and closed in on an agreement for uranium supply to India, as PM Narendra Modi held talks with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.Modi announced that India would get into a long-term arrangement for supply of uranium from Uzbekistan, a major regional producer and exporter. Both sides agreed to establish a foreign minister-level coordination council to guide all aspects of cooperation under the elevated partnership.Following the talks that focused on expanding cooperation in defence and security, trade and investment, critical minerals, AI, agriculture and health, the 2 sides signed 11 MoUs. Areas covered included culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism and restoration of Buddhist sites in the Central Asian country.Modi also underscored the need for zero tolerance against terrorism and extremism, saying a stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.The leaders endorsed growing defence cooperation between the 2 countries, including through regular exchanges, capacity-building and joint activities, and expressed their commitment in a joint statement to address common security challenges by further strengthening such cooperation.Going forward, Modi said, both sides will promote direct linkages, co-production, and co-development between the defense industries of both nations."Close defense and security cooperation between our two countries reflects our deep mutual trust," said the PM.Outlining an ambitious agenda to move forward with “speed and tangible results” in this new phase of our partnership, the PM also said in his media statement that both sides will work systematically on market access, connectivity, banking, and payment systems to achieve the target of $ 5 billion trade by 2030.“We will work together to boost win-win cooperation in infrastructure development. Cooperation in Digital Public Infrastructure, AI, critical minerals, clean energy, space, and nuclear energy is making our relationship future-ready,” said Modi, adding that Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia, and at the heart of India’s engagement with the region.Both sides believe that while India is one of Uzbekistan’s top 10 trading partners, their annual trade of $ 1.32 billion remains significantly below its true potential.In the meeting, the leaders agreed to undertake joint measures to broaden the range of goods traded between the two countries, remove non-tariff barriers, and promote industrial cooperation with a view to further increasing bilateral trade turnover, according to the joint statement. They also decided to create a Joint Working Group to address non-tariff issues and investment barriers.There was focus on Global South cooperation with Modi saying that Uzbekistan’s highest honour for a foreign leader that was conferred on him by the president had left India with the added responsibility of working with Uzbekistan as “Global South partners for the betterment of humanity”.“Both sides agreed to work together to preserve and protect the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, especially for the interests of the developing countries,” said the joint statement. Modi and Mirziyoyev discussed a recently concluded jointly feasibility study for Uzbekistan-India Preferential Trade Agreement, directing officials to explore the next steps on a time bound basis.On international cooperation, the leaders called for comprehensive UN reforms that would reflect contemporary global realities and to make it more representative and effective in dealing with issues of international peace and security, with Uzbekistan reaffirming its support for India’s candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council.The leaders explored cooperation in the fields of geology, mining, nuclear energy, industrial cooperation, and critical & strategic minerals, including projects for the processing of mineral resources, according to the joint statement. The 2 sides also announced partnerships between their cities and states, with Modi saying that these arrangements will continuously enhance direct connections in urban management, industry, education, tourism, and culture.
Article Summary: Modi announced that India would get into a long-term arrangement for supply of uranium from Uzbekistan. Both sides agreed to establish a foreign minister-level coordination council to guide all aspects of cooperation under the elevated partnership. Areas covered included culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism and restoration of Buddhist sites.

Article Title: IISc eco-friendly foam moves from lab to market; TOI story drew industry

BENGALURU: An eco-friendly bio-based foam developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science ( IISc ), is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation, with Absolute Cold LLP working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging.The foam, developed by Prof Suryasarathi Bose and Prof Subodh Kumar, along with the team comprising Sampath Parasuram, Akshay Sunil Salvi, Supriya H, Sandeep Kumar Singh and Amit Malakar, is an alternative to conventional polyurethane (PU) foam, which is widely used for insulation but is difficult to recycle after use.The IISc material was designed to combine the properties needed for insulation with a more sustainable approach to what happens to the material at the end of its life. The journey from laboratory to industry also had a link to TOI.Bose said a report on the development published by TOI on Nov 11, 2024, helped bring a potential industry partner on board. “Your [TOI] article brought in a potential licensee on board and helped take the technology to market. Absolute Cold director saw your story and reached out to us,” he said.The original IISc work involved making the foam using epoxidised fatty acids derived from non-edible oils and polyphenol-based materials derived from tea leaves.The researchers also incorporated a chemical structure that allows the material to be reprocessed, rather than simply being discarded after use.Absolute Cold, which works in the cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics sector, subsequently became interested in the technology. The company is now working towards translating the laboratory material into a product for applications where maintaining temperature during storage and transport is critical.This could include packaging used to transport pharmaceuticals and other temperature-sensitive products. Such packaging needs to provide insulation while also being lightweight and strong enough to withstand handling and transportation. Its environmental impact after use is an increasing consideration as well.The move is the latest step in Bose’s broader work on more sustainable polymeric materials. His research has included efforts to find ways of reusing or upcycling plastics that are otherwise difficult to recycle, with the aim of keeping materials in use for longer rather than sending them to waste.For IISc, the foam's progress also shows the less visible part of academic innovation: getting a material developed in a laboratory into a form that industry can manufacture and customers can use. The licensing and scale-up process can require changes to the formulation, manufacturing process and product design even after the underlying research has been demonstrated.The next test, therefore, is whether the foam can be produced at commercial scale while retaining the insulation, strength and durability demonstrated during development. Its performance in actual cold-chain applications will ultimately determine whether the IISc innovation can become a practical alternative to conventional foams.For a material conceived around the problem of what happens to foam after its useful life, that commercial journey is as important as the laboratory breakthrough itself.
Article Summary: Bio-based foam developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation. Absolute Cold LLP is working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging. The journey from laboratory to industry also had a link to TOI.

Defaulted amounts will now be deducted directly from monthly salaries and transferred to the bank accounts of the estranged wives or children concerned,” Majhi’s office said in a statement.The order followed repeated complaints from women in distress reaching the chief minister’s office. “Several male employees failed to provide maintenance grants or alimony even after divorce, ignoring explicit court instructions. On average, two to three such complaints are received during the CM’s grievance hearings,” the statement noted.The CMO added: “Despite repeated judicial directives, many women and children were left without financial support.The chief minister has taken a stern stance against government employees who defy court orders and neglect their families.”Majhi himself underscored the moral dimension of the directive. “It is unacceptable for government employees to act unjustly towards their spouses and children while drawing salaries from the state exchequer,” he said.Following the order, the government issued detailed guidelines. Once a court order is received, the departmental drawing and disbursement officer (DDO) will deduct the specified amount from the employee’s salary bill and transfer it electronically to the beneficiaries. The CM has further directed that such cases be integrated into the state’s centralized human resource management system (HRMS) to ensure automated compliance and eliminate delays.Officials said they will track such errant husbands from complaints received by victims.Legal experts welcomed the initiative. “Salary deductions will ensure that court orders are not reduced to mere paperwork,” said senior advocate Pramod Mishra.Women’s rights activists also hailed the decision. “For years, women have struggled to enforce maintenance orders. This mechanism will bring relief and dignity to many households,” said activist Sunita Patnaik. She added: “By linking alimony enforcement to the HRMS system, the government hopes to prevent harassment of affected women and children.The move will not only uphold judicial authority but also ease the distress of families who often face prolonged battles for rightful support.”
Article Summary: The order followed repeated complaints from women in distress reaching the chief minister’s office. Article Title: Constitutional norm for jurist as SC judge unmet: Justice Bhuyan

NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a Supreme Court judge, Sunday said though Article 124(3) permitted appointment of ‘distinguished jurists’ as judges of the apex court, it was regrettable that this provision had remained one of our Constitution’s unused mandates.“No jurist has been appointed so far to SC though Constitution has completed more than 76 years,” he said, adding that either Centre earlier or the collegium thereafter was not convinced about the depth in Indian academia or had not seriously explored Article 124(3) so far.Addressing the convocation of LLM students at National Law University, Delhi, Justice Bhuyan said, “No legal academic has yet been appointed as a judge of SC, despite there being brilliant minds who could have made a substantial contribution had they become part of the bench.”Addressing the ‘lack of practical experience’ argument against elevation of jurists as judges, he said, “SC is not only the highest adjudicatory body but it is the moral, legal and constitutional conscience-keeper of the nation. It is above technicalities.”The objective behind appointing ‘distinguished jurists’ as SC judges is to diversify as they “can be a great value addition to the bench”, he said, adding, “By his or her scholarship, he or she can make a visible contribution to the decision-making process at the top level.Participation of renowned legal academia and scholars would have a defining impact on the judicial functioning of Supreme Court.”He said academics were routinely appointed as judges to constitutional courts in US, UK, Canada and Kenya. In America, they could practise as long as it did not interfere with academic sessions, but this practice was opposed here by rule 49 of Bar Council of India, he said.In US, Felix Frankfurter became the first jurist to be an SC judge, picked by Theodore Roosevelt in 1939. Thereafter, several from legal academia have been appointed as US supreme court judges, many of whom had teaching experience prior to this role.

Article Title: Diabetes impacts men, women differently: Study
Article Text:
Study finds type 2 diabetes complications differ by gender: men face higher heart and kidney risks, women more likely to develop mental health conditions.

Mental health risks are higher for women with diabetes as compared to men

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For men, type 2 diabetes more often sets the stage for heart and kidney disease; for women, the greater threat appears to be mental health problems, a new study tracking nearly 29,000 patients has found.The study, published in PLOS Medicine, followed 28,720 people newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes between 2010 and 2020 using linked primary and secondary healthcare records in the UK. Researchers used a multi-state analysis to track the order and timing of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, end-stage renal disease and mental health conditions over a median follow-up of 6.8 years. Women were more likely than men to be diagnosed with a mental health condition.Women were more likely than men to be diagnosed with a mental health condition, including anxiety, depression or somatoform disorders, after developing diabetes. Such conditions were recorded in 8.1% of women compared with 5.3% of men.Men, meanwhile, were more likely to develop cardiovascular disease or end-stage renal disease, with 8.4% following this trajectory compared with 5.3% of women.Senior endocrinologist Prof Ravinder Goswami of All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) said diabetes can affect men and women differently.Men may develop diabetes at a younger age, while women with diabetes lose the natural protection against heart disease that is usually seen before menopause. The study also found that women with diabetes may have a higher risk of problems related to memory, thinking and mental health.However, he cautioned that these problems may not be caused by diabetes alone, as cognitive and neuropsychiatric problems are generally more common in women. He said doctors should, therefore, watch for these issues while managing diabetes.Hypertension was the most common complication after type-2 diabetes across all age groups and in both sexes. It affected 21.1% of men and 20.2% of women. Men also experienced most complications earlier than women, while women generally had a later onset of events.The study linked diabetes, mental health and mortality, finding that people who developed a mental health condition after diabetes died earlier. Among those with the same disease trajectory, men died on average nine years younger than women.Despite this, women had higher average healthcare utilisation and long-term prescribing than men. The researchers said the lower healthcare use among men in the high-risk mental health trajectory could point to gaps in engagement with healthcare services.The findings point to the need for sex-specific diabetes care, including routine mental health screening, particularly for younger women, and earlier cardiovascular and kidney monitoring for men.The researchers further added that tracking the sequence and timing of complications could help identify patients at higher risk and enable earlier intervention. However, as an observational study, the findings cannot establish cause and effect, and differences in mental health diagnoses may partly reflect healthcare-seeking behaviour.
Article Summary: Mental health risks are higher for women with diabetes as compared to men. Study followed 28,720 people newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes between 2010 and 2020 using linked primary and secondary healthcare records in the UK. Researchers used a multi-state analysis to track the order and timing of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, end-stage renal disease and mental health conditions.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said India and Uzbekistan have decided to elevate their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, setting a target of $5 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.Addressing a joint press meet with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, PM Modi said the two countries share common aspirations and are looking to expand cooperation across trade, technology, defence, energy, infrastructure and other strategic sectors.“Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia and at the heart of India's engagement with the region,” the Prime Minister said.He noted that 2026 marks 15 years of the India-Uzbekistan strategic partnership and said the two countries were now looking to give their relationship a broader and more ambitious framework.“India and Uzbekistan have deep similarities in their thinking and aspirations. Uzbekistan's medicinal herbs and India's expertise in Ayurveda form a natural combination,” PM said.PM Modi also announced that India and Uzbekistan would establish three sister-city and sister-state arrangements to expand cooperation beyond the national capitals.“We aim to ensure that our partnership is not limited merely to our national capitals; therefore, we are establishing partnerships between our cities and states,” he said.He also highlighted the potential for cooperation between Uzbekistan's New Tashkent project and India's GIFT City.“Mega-projects like 'New Tashkent' are underway in your country, while in India, we have developed GIFT City in Gujarat. Article Title: 1 in 5 food samples fails: Why so few cases end in conviction
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Nearly one in five food samples tested across India was found to be non-conforming in 2025-26, even as only 4.8% of food safety violations ended in convictions, highlighting gaps in enforcement and staffing across states, according to data analysed by Richa Gandhi.The share of non-conforming food samples has remained around 20% over the past five years, despite a steady rise in the number of samples tested. In 2025-26, authorities analysed 2,23,808 samples, of which 40,023 were found to be non-conforming.The proportion of non-conforming samples stood at 17.9% in 2025-26, down from 20.2% in 2024-25 and 19.8% in 2023-24. It had peaked at 25.1% in 2022-23.At the same time, the conviction rate has gradually increased, rising from 2% in 2021-22 to 4.8% in 2025-26. However, monetary penalties remain the more common form of action against violators.Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest proportion of non-conforming samples among the states listed, with 52% of the nearly 40,000 samples tested in 2025-26 found to be non-conforming.The state analysed 39,519 samples and found 20,021 to be non-conforming.Haryana followed with 31%, while Jharkhand recorded 28%, Rajasthan 27%, Puducherry 22% and Himachal Pradesh 20%.Tamil Nadu analysed the highest number of samples among the larger states, with nearly 45,000 tests, and also recorded the highest conviction rate among those states.Chandigarh recorded the highest conviction rate overall at 32.1%, followed by Tamil Nadu at 21.5%, Kerala at 17.7%, Haryana at 16% and Delhi at 14.7%.The data points to a sharp gap between the scale of food safety violations detected through testing and the number of cases that ultimately result in convictions.Shortages in food safety personnel are another major constraint on monitoring and enforcement.Bihar has the largest gap among the states listed, with 91 of its 105 sanctioned food safety posts vacant. Jharkhand has 74 vacancies against 77 sanctioned posts, while Chhattisgarh has 70 vacancies against 125 posts.Andhra Pradesh has 68 vacancies out of 145 sanctioned posts, followed by Uttarakhand with 65 vacancies out of 57 sanctioned posts, according to the data.Haryana has 57 vacancies against 367 sanctioned posts, while Odisha has 57 vacancies against 147. Tripura has 52 vacancies against 23 sanctioned posts, Manipur 50 against 34 and Sikkim 50 against four.The staffing gaps limit the ability of state authorities to regularly inspect establishments, collect samples and pursue violations through the enforcement process.Milk and dairy products, ghee, spices, edible oils and sweets remain among the food categories frequently flagged in regulatory actions and recent cases.In one major case, ghee supplied for the preparation of Tirupati laddus came under scrutiny after samples failed quality tests amid allegations of adulteration with vegetable oils and animal fats.Milk and milk products such as paneer and khoya have also faced increased scrutiny. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ordered a nationwide crackdown between September and October following cases involving alleged detergent and urea adulteration in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.In Punjab, 47% of milk, cheese and dairy samples reportedly failed tests over a three-year period. Cheese was identified as particularly vulnerable to adulteration involving starch and chemical additives, with 255 of 531 samples failing tests in 2024-25 alone.Spices such as turmeric and chilli powder have also been the subject of seizures over adulteration involving synthetic colours, wood dust and other unsafe fillers.Edible oils are another concern, with cheaper palm oil being used to adulterate more expensive oils such as groundnut and mustard oil.Sweets and khoya are also regularly identified as high-risk categories in FSSAI advisories during festive periods, when demand rises sharply.The figures underline the challenge facing India's food safety system: while testing has expanded and the detection of violations remains significant, limited staffing and the relatively low rate of convictions continue to constrain enforcement.
Article Summary: Nearly one in five food samples tested across India was found to be non- conforming in 2025-26. Only 4.8% of food safety violations ended in convictions, according to data analysed by Richa Gandhi. Shortages in food safety staff hamper monitoring and enforcement.

Article Title: High-level review meet held over proposed 'ARISE' project for coastal projection and climate resilience in Odisha

A high-level meeting on the proposed Adaptive Resilience Investment in Coastal Systems on Economics (ARISE) Project was held on Saturday at Lok Seva Bhawan to deliberate on a comprehensive and long-term strategy for protecting Odisha's coastline, enhancing climate resilience and promoting sustainable economic development in coastal areas.Odisha Minister of Revenue & Disaster Management, Suresh Pujari, who chaired the meeting, emphasised the need for a comprehensive approach to coastal management that combines coastal protection, environmental conservation, livelihood security, biodiversity protection and economic sustainability. He stressed that the ARISE Project should contribute towards strengthening the resilience of coastal communities and ecosystems against the growing impacts of climate change.A preliminary assessment of Odisha's 573-km coastline has been undertaken jointly by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA). Consultations have also been held with ADB and the Departments of Water Resources, Forest, Fisheries & Animal Resources Development & Revenue & Disaster Management on key issues relating to coastal erosion, sediment management, protection of coastal villages and safeguarding the lives and livelihoods of coastal communities.Based on these consultations, ADB and OSDMA have prepared a preliminary report, which was discussed in detail during the meeting.It was informed that ADB (Asian Development Bank) has also been working with the State Governments of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu on coastal protection initiatives. The first phase of the coastal protection project in Karnataka has already been completed. The Minister informed that after completion of the final assessment and report for Odisha, the ARISE Project would be taken up in a phased manner, with appropriate interventions to strengthen coastal protection across the State.The meeting discussed integrated measures to address coastal erosion along Odisha's coastline. Emphasis was placed on scientific & technology-driven interventions to reduce erosion, protect vulnerable coastal stretches and strengthen long-term coastal resilience.The development of Odisha's Blue Economy was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on harnessing the State's vast marine resources and economic potential in a sustainable and responsible manner. The approach would seek to generate greater livelihood and economic opportunities for coastal communities while contributing to the State's overall economic growth, a release said.The meeting also focused on promoting Climate-Resilient Coastal Tourism in view of the increasing impacts of climate change and natural hazards. Discussions centred on developing sustainable tourism models that balance economic opportunities with environmental conservation and strengthen the resilience of coastal tourism infrastructure and communities.Coastal Protection and Sediment Management were identified as key components of the proposed interventions. The meeting emphasised the need to understand the natural dynamics of Odisha's coastline and adopt scientifically informed approaches for managing sediment movement and deposition. Strengthening natural coastal defence systems and undertaking suitable protective measures at vulnerable locations were also discussed.For effective implementation of the ARISE Project, special emphasis was laid on Institutional Strengthening, Capacity Building and Advanced Technological Systems. The meeting discussed strengthening the institutional capacity of departments and agencies involved in coastal management, enhancing the technical skills of officials and personnel, and promoting knowledge and experience sharing among stakeholders.The use of modern technology, real-time data and digital platforms for effective coastal management was also emphasised. An integrated technological monitoring system for tracking coastal erosion, improving hazard forecasting, supporting data-driven decision-making and strengthening preparedness and response mechanisms was identified as an important component of the long-term strategy, a release further said.The meeting emphasised that the ARISE Project should adopt a long-term, scientific, integrated and sustainable approach to enhance climate resilience along Odisha's extensive coastline while simultaneously strengthening environmental protection, disaster resilience, coastal livelihoods and economic development.Special Relief Commissioner and Managing Director, OSDMA, Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, senior officials of OSDMA and senior officials of the Asian Development Bank attended the meeting, a release added.
Article Summary: High-level meeting held on proposed Adaptive Resilience Investment in Coastal Systems on Economics (ARISE) Project. Minister of Revenue & Disaster Management, Suresh Pujari, who chaired the meeting emphasised the need for a comprehensive approach to coastal management.

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan. The scheme is aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.

Article Title: Milk procurement price raised to Rs 44 per litre in Tamil Nadu

CHENNAI: The TVK govt on Monday announced a further Rs 3 per litre hike in the procurement price of milk, taking the rate paid to milk producers from Rs 41 to Rs 44. The move is aimed at benefiting more than 3.16 lakh producers supplying milk to primary dairy cooperative societies across Tamil Nadu.Announcing the decision under Rule 110 in the Assembly, chief minister C Joseph Vijay said the govt had decided to increase the procurement price considering the rising cost of cattle feed and other inputs.“Following the earlier increase from Rs 38 to Rs 41 per litre, the government has now decided to further increase the procurement price by Rs 3 to Rs 44 per litre,” Vijay said.The latest hike comes just days after the government announced an increase in the procurement price on Aug 19. The earlier revision included a Rs 1 increase through cooperative societies and an increase in the government incentive from Rs 3 to Rs 5 per litre, taking the overall procurement price from Rs 38 to Rs 41.The latest decision follows representations from various cooperative milk producers’ welfare associations and milk producers, who sought a further revision citing a sharp increase in the cost of green fodder, dry fodder, bran, oil cakes and other farm inputs.The govt said it would fully compensate Aavin for the additional expenditure arising from the latest procurement price increase.The hike will impose an additional burden of Rs 60 crore a month and Rs 720 crore annually on the government.“The government has taken this decision keeping the welfare of milk producers in mind,” the CM said.

Article Title: Nearly one in three voters struck off Delhi SIR draft roll
Article Text:
47.5 lakh Delhi voters missing from draft SIR roll (File Photo)





NEW DELHI: Nearly one in three registered voters of Delhi have been struck off the draft Special Intensive Revision (SIR) electoral roll which was published by Election Commission Monday morning.The draft rolls include the names of 97,53,577 voters while names of 47,56,722 among 1.45 crore registered voters are missing from the SIR rolls because they failed to submit their voter details during the one and a half month long voters verification exercise conducted across 70 assembly constituencies of the capital.Election officials said many voters were not found at their registered addresses, while others had shifted within Delhi or moved out of the city.According to figures released by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, enumeration forms of 67.2% of Delhi’s electorate were submitted and digitised. The remaining 32.8% were categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others (ASDDO).TOI on July 26 reported that around 20% of the registered voters were not found at their addresses during the door to door verification, and on August 18 it reported that nearly one in three voters of Delhi were likely to be struck off the draft electoral roll.Election Commission figures as on August 31 show that 67.2% of Delhi’s 1,45,10,299 (around 97.5 lakh) registered voters were verified. The remaining 47.5 lakh voters were marked “uncollectable” and categorised as ASDDO voters.Voters whose names are missing from the draft roll will be able to file claims and objections between Aug 31 and Sept 30. During this period, officials will closely examine the claims for inclusion in the electoral roll, while booth-level officers (BLOs) will conduct field visits to verify them. Once the details are found to be in order, the voters’ names will be included in the final SIR electoral roll, scheduled to be published on Nov 4.The SIR exercise was launched on June 30 to update Delhi’s electoral rolls and remove ineligible entries. Originally scheduled to conclude on July 29, it was extended three times. During the exercise, around 13,000 BLOs distributed enumeration forms across all 13 districts, according to Delhi chief electoral officer’s office.Details regarding the assembly wise distribution of the names of deleted voters are awaited.
Article Summary: Nearly one in three registered voters of Delhi have been struck off the draft Special Intensive Revision (SIR) electoral roll. The draft rolls include the names of 97,53,577 voters while names of 47,56,722 among 1.45 crore registered voters are missing from the SIR rolls.

Article Title: India vs China: How their nuclear-capable missile arsenals compare
Article Text:
The Agni family of missiles are designed to carry the weight of India's strategic weapons. (Image credit: DRDO)

China Reveals Airborne Nuclear Strike System As Xi Flexes Strategic Firepower | WATCH

Indian and Chinese strategic missiles

China and India, Asia's two most powerful countries, have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles are strategic weapons that act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). This prohibitive concept states that two nuclear armed powers will not use these weapons on each other, as the use of such a weapon will ensure a retaliatory strike, thereby increasing the cost for the attacker. India and China's strategic missile arsenals now bear resemblance, but also at the same time there are differences in capability. The two countries also are also employing different philosophies for the use of these weapons, as the US Naval Institute states that China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.While India is building its strategic missile arsenal to act as an insurance against attacks from nuclear weapons armed entities. This concept is enshrined in India's no first use policy for nuclear weapons. India depends on the Agni family of missiles for its land based nuclear deterrence, while China depends on the Dongfeng series.At the shorter end of the spectrum, China's road-mobile DF-16 offers a range between 800 and 1,000 kilometres, giving it reach over Taiwan and much of the western Pacific.India's comparable system, the Agni-I, delivers a range of 700 to 900 kilometres, and while it lacks the DF-16's higher payload capacity of up to 1,500 kilograms, it remains a reliable, road and rail-mobile system tailored specifically for shorter-range contingencies closer to India's borders.Moving up the ladder in terms of range and capability, China's DF-21, one of the People's Liberation Army's most storied missiles, offers a range of up to 2,500 kilometres and famously spawned the world's first anti-ship ballistic missile variant, the DF-21D. India's Agni-II sits in a similar bracket, with a declared range of 2,000 to 3,500 kilometres, and has long been described as central to India's deterrence posture with respect to China, despite New Delhi's insistence that its missile programme is not aimed at any single adversary.At the intermediate range, China's DF-26, capable of striking targets over 5,000 kilometres away, including American bases in Guam, sits close in class to India's Agni-III, which offers a declared range of 3,000 to 5,000 kilometres and has been noted for a circular error probable of just around 40 metres, making it among the most accurate missiles in its class. This accuracy allows India to rely on smaller-yield warheads while still achieving high lethality, a design philosophy that keeps the system relatively compact for its range class.Where the comparison becomes genuinely interesting is at the intercontinental tier. China's DF-31A, a solid-fuel ICBM, boasts a range in excess of 11,000 kilometres. India's Agni-V, its first genuine intercontinental system, offers a declared range of 7,000 to 8,000 kilometres, though some Chinese analysts have suggested its true reach may extend closer to 8,000 kilometres once payload adjustments are factored in. Both missiles share canisterised, road-mobile configurations, a design choice that improves survivability and reduces launch preparation time.At the very top sits China's DF-41, believed to carry ten to twelve MIRV warheads across a range of 12,000 to 15,000 kilometres, making it one of the longest-range missiles in the world. India's answer, the still-developing Agni-VI, is expected to offer a comparable range of as much as 10,000 kilometres, with reports suggesting it could eventually be fitted with MIRV warheads and even a submarine-launched variant, mirroring China's own efforts to build a survivable, multi-domain nuclear triad.Taken together, the comparison suggests India has broadly kept pace with China across most range categories, even as Beijing continues to hold an edge in payload flexibility, warhead multiplicity, and the sheer scale of its overall missile inventory.
Article Summary: India and China have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD) China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.

Article Title: Mumbaikars to pay more for autos, taxis as new fares kick in tonight; minimum fare up by Rs 1-2
Article Text:
Auto-rickshaw and taxi fares will increase across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region starting September 1.





MUMBAI: Auto-rickshaw and taxi rides will cost more across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) from midnight on Monday, with revised fares coming into effect from September 1. The state transport department on Sunday released the new tariff cards, giving commuters and drivers a reference point until meters are recalibrated.The minimum autorickshaw fare has been increased from Rs 26 to Rs 27 for the first 1.5 km. The subsequent fare has been fixed at Rs 18.22 per km, rounded off to the nearest rupee. For taxis, the minimum fare has risen from Rs 31 to Rs 33 for 1.5 km, while the subsequent fare will be Rs 21.90 per km.The increase will mean that a 10-km auto ride will cost Rs 182, up from Rs 171, while a taxi ride over the same distance will cost Rs 219, compared with Rs 207 earlier.The revised fares will apply across Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Mira-Bhayander, Kalyan and the rest of the MMR.Under the new tariff, an auto ride covering 2 km will cost Rs 36, compared with Rs 34 earlier, while a 5-km journey will cost Rs 91 against Rs 86. For taxis, the fare for 2 km will rise to Rs 44 from Rs 41, while a 5-km ride will cost Rs 110, compared with Rs 103 earlier.Passengers travelling in AC black-and-yellow taxis will have to pay 10% more than the basic black-and-yellow taxi fare.A 25% additional fare will continue to apply for journeys between midnight and 5am.The department has also revised shared-ride fares. The minimum shared-auto fare will now be Rs 12, while the minimum shared-taxi fare will be Rs 11, with both increasing by Re 1.Waiting charges will range between Rs 1 and Rs 2 per minute, depending on the distance covered, officials said.The revised tariff cards will remain valid for three months, during which meters will be recalibrated. The recalibration process is expected to begin this week in phases and continue until November 30.Transport officials have advised commuters to ask drivers for the tariff card or keep a copy with them to check the applicable fare and avoid disputes during the transition period.Driver unions have welcomed the fare revision, while commuter groups have raised concerns about the additional burden on household budgets, particularly for those who regularly rely on autos and taxis for daily travel.
Article Summary: Auto-rickshaw and taxi rides will cost more across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) from midnight on Monday. The revised fares will apply across Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Mira-Bhayander, Kalyan and the rest of the MMR. The state transport department on Sunday released the new tariff cards.
